pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

- Renames the `InstrumentationMiddleware` to `MetricsMiddleware`
- Moves the contextual logger from the `Instrumentation/Metrics middleware` to the `LoggerMiddleware`

**Why do we need this feature?**

Better naming and consistency.

**Who is this feature for?**

Plugins platform.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

- Automatically closes linked issue when the Pull Request is merged.

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [x] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-a-whats-new-document), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: Plugins: Chore: Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware

raw_findings.body: All log calls routed through FromContext are recorded on a throwaway TestLogger instance, so the injected fake observes zero calls; assertions on captured logs silently pass/fail incorrectly and the fake cannot verify the new FromContext-based logging path at all.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test fake loses observability of production log calls made through the newly introduced FromContext code path, making log assertions impossible or misleading.
raw_findings.impact: All log calls routed through FromContext are recorded on a throwaway TestLogger instance, so the injected fake observes zero calls; assertions on captured logs silently pass/fail incorrectly and the fake cannot verify the new FromContext-based logging path at all.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new FromContext implementation copies the New() pattern of allocating a fresh TestLogger instead of preserving the receiver used for capture.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return the receiver (`return f`) from TestLogger.FromContext so calls remain observable on the injected instance, or return a child logger that shares the parent's Logs counters.
raw_findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance, discarding captured log calls
raw_findings.trigger: A test injects a *TestLogger into code that logs via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) (e.g. the new LoggerMiddleware path m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)) and then asserts on f.InfoLogs.Calls or f.InfoLogs.Message.

raw_findings.body: The test file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and its body updated to newMetricsMiddleware, but the enclosing test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware (visible in the hunk header), so the type it exercises can no longer be located by name and the rename is incomplete, defeating the PR's stated naming-consistency goal.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale naming misleads reviewers and breaks name-based test selection/discovery for the renamed middleware.
raw_findings.impact: The test file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and its body updated to newMetricsMiddleware, but the enclosing test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware (visible in the hunk header), so the type it exercises can no longer be located by name and the rename is incomplete, defeating the PR's stated naming-consistency goal.
raw_findings.root_cause: The rename from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware updated the file name and constructor call but left the test function identifier stale.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the test function TestInstrumentationMiddleware to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed type and file.
raw_findings.title: Test function name still references removed InstrumentationMiddleware after rename to MetricsMiddleware
raw_findings.trigger: A developer runs `go test -run TestMetricsMiddleware` or greps for tests covering MetricsMiddleware after this rename PR merges.

raw_findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on this middleware for pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields (the explicit logParams were deleted from logRequest), yet no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added; a regression that drops these attributes from plugin request logs would merge undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of structured log fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) on plugin request logs would not be caught by any test.
raw_findings.impact: LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on this middleware for pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields (the explicit logParams were deleted from logRequest), yet no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added; a regression that drops these attributes from plugin request logs would merge undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The contextual-logger logic was extracted into a new middleware without carrying over or adding tests that assert the attributes it injects.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that runs ContextualLoggerMiddleware over QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics and asserts the expected key/value pairs are present in the context via log.WithContextualAttributes/FromContext.
raw_findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage for contextual attribute injection
raw_findings.trigger: A future refactor changes instrumentContext, the middleware wiring order in CreateMiddlewares, or which endpoints call instrumentContext; the CI test suite is run.

raw_findings.body: Adding a method to the exported Logger interface is a compile-breaking change for every existing implementer of the interface; consumers of the pkg/plugins packages that supply their own Logger will fail to build until they add FromContext.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Downstream implementations of plog.Logger stop compiling without notice in the PR description or docs.
raw_findings.impact: Adding a method to the exported Logger interface is a compile-breaking change for every existing implementer of the interface; consumers of the pkg/plugins packages that supply their own Logger will fail to build until they add FromContext.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new required method was added to a widely-implemented exported interface instead of an additive optional interface.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either accept and document the breaking change in the PR/changelog, or introduce FromContext via a separate optional interface (e.g. ContextualLogger) that callers type-assert, keeping Logger stable.
raw_findings.title: Adding FromContext to exported plugins/log.Logger interface breaks external implementers
raw_findings.trigger: Any code outside this repository (or an unupdated in-repo fake) that implements github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/plugins/log.Logger is compiled against this change.
